To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a series of isostructural Ni4Ln2 compounds (Ln = Gg, Tb, Dy and Ho) were prepared, and the Tb- and Ho-containing derivatives showed SMM behavior.

we have synthesized a series of Ni4Ln2 compounds, where Ln = Gd, Dy, Tb, and Ho, with an unprecedented 4d-4f topology consisting of two dicubane units and that the Ni-Tb (2) and Ni-Ho (4) complexes show SMM behavior.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and structural characterization of a new family of isostructural hexanucler Ni4Ln2 and Ni4Y complexes (Ln = Gg, Tb, Dy and Ho) with a defect-dicuban topology.
the assembly of novel 3d-3d and 3d-5f metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with a defect-dicubanide topology.
the design and synthesis of novel Ni-Dy and Ni-Ln complexes (Ln = Tb and Ho) and their magnetic studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ni-Tb, Ni-Ho, and Ni-Dy species exhibit slow relaxation of magnetization, while the Ni-Gd and Ni-Y derivatives show no SMM behavior.
the slow magnetic relaxation in these Ni4Ln2 compounds is a result of the interplay of the magnetic anisotropy of the lanthanide ions with the Ni(II) ions and the ligand field.
the SMM behavior in 2 and 4 is a consequence of the presence of the Ln(III) ions, and the slow relaxation in 3 is a combination of both the Ni2+ and Dy3+ ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic behavior of 2-5 is a result of the interplay of the Ni(II) ions' magnetic anisotropy with the Tb(III) or Ho(III) ions' anisotropy and exchange coupling.
the Ni4Ln2 compounds are the first examples to display the slow magnetic relaxation of magnetization for Tb(III) or Ho(III).
the Ni-Tb, Ni-Dy, and Ni-Ho samples show slow relaxation of the magnetic moment with a zero dc field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a defect-dicubanoid core in a hexanuclear Ni-Ln complex is a promising platform for the design of single-molecule magnets (SMMs).
the Ni4Y2 species is a good reference material to investigate the magnetic behavior of the Ni4Ln2 derivatives (Ln = Gda, Tb, Dy and Ho).
the magnetic properties of these 3d- 4f metal clusters can be tailored by the choice of the lanthanide ions.
